obligations.statement: Each work item has one authoritative rendered contract derived from its acceptance selection.
obligations.source: Problem statement; Solution and scope; LIFE-D1: "The canonical contract is the field's selection after resolution. There is no separate editable review copy."

parts.statement: The acceptance field selects the contract, including citations rather than copied spec text.
Rendering places the full description under its own heading and resolved criteria under the acceptance-criteria heading.
Rendering depends only on description, acceptance field, and named spec.
No separate editable review copy exists.
Existing consumers recover criteria only from the acceptance-criteria section.

obligations.statement: The renderer resolves citations and text deterministically under the specified grammar and remains compatible with spec-lint.
obligations.source: LIFE-D1 resolution rules and its final compatibility paragraph.

parts.statement: Citations resolve complete nonempty entries in field order, with blank-line, comma, whitespace, continuation, and working-directory behavior preserved.
Text and mixed inputs receive stable unique grammar-valid IDs while explicit IDs survive.
Invalid references, unreadable or unparseable specs, and ID collisions are refused with the offending identifier or path and cause.
Editing a cited entry changes every citing item's rendering without item edits.
The workcli and spec-lint grammars remain marked counterparts.
The two grammars remain compatible beyond the cases sampled by their shared fixture.
Component specs define the exact generated-ID spelling and refusal payloads before implementation.

obligations.statement: Every item is classified as spec-born or tracker-born and uses the corresponding attackable document and record workflow.

parts.statement: All-citation items attack the whole spec; any full-text line makes the item attack its rendering.
An empty selection remains unclaimable even when the spec has been attacked.
The tracker-born workflow renders, attacks, checks, commits the canonical paths, and then attests.
The generated attack directory is tracked, has a placeholder, and is exempt from authored-prose doc-lint.
A direct edit of the generated rendering is not treated as an amendment; the item is updated and rerendered instead.
Unchanged valid files and evidence are reused without a new model round, including when only attestation is missing.
Attack or checker failure leaves no committed generated files or attestation and is retried on the next invocation.

obligations.statement: Attestation binds an item to the current attacked bytes and only records canonically closed evidence.

parts.statement: The marker contains a parseable timestamp.
The marker contains the digest of the attacked document's bytes.
A valid record produces one idempotent attestation under repeated or concurrent requests.
Every binding or closure violation named in LIFE-D3 is refused without writing a marker.
A content-preserving rename preserves attestation after references and filename binding are updated.
Malformed markers do not count and unreadable marker sources cause named refusals.
The facade checks binding and closure without duplicating semantic or lens judgments.

obligations.statement: Amendments invalidate prior evidence and require a full new attack before use.

parts.statement: A tracker-born acceptance or description change that changes rendering invalidates its attestation.
Any spec-byte change invalidates the spec record and citing attestations, while a spec-born description-only change does not.
Acceptance-field amendments use the `work acceptance set --why` trail.
The amended document is rerendered where needed, fully re-attacked, committed, and re-attested before use.
Dispatch and criteria-indicting halt instructions state the quality-standard and before-use amendment rules.

obligations.statement: Lifecycle gates enforce the LIFE-D5 transition matrix and structural-role behavior.

parts.statement: Creation and discovery allow rough or empty criteria.
Every open-to-in-progress verb applies the noun and triviality rules, while an already-in-progress claim is a no-op.
PR delivery requires resolvable criteria and requires current attestation exactly when LIFE-D5 specifies.
Review emission applies the review row of LIFE-D5.
Verdict posting applies the posting row of LIFE-D5.
Gates do not classify criterion prose.
A design child bypasses claim and delivery gates while present records remain subject to the repository record gate.
Installing the facade does not rewrite existing items.
Every applicable refusal gives the prescribed remedy for empty criteria or missing attestation.
An implementation placeholder is refused at claim.
An item with no recognized noun or structural role is refused by type at claim and delivery.
Claim and delivery name the exact empty, resolution, and attestation causes.
An implementation placeholder is retired when the spec manifest expands.

obligations.statement: Review emission and verdict posting use only the current rendered contract and preserve the judged bytes.

parts.statement: Emission requires exact equality with a fresh rendering and records those bytes.
Posting requires equality with both recorded judged input and a fresh rendering, using content rather than amendment history.
Posting refuses a round with no recorded judged input.
Review emission refuses a failure to obtain a current rendering and never falls back to an unchecked file.
Verdict posting refuses a failure to obtain a current rendering and never falls back to an unchecked file.
The poster extracts criteria only from the acceptance-criteria section.
A no-item target retains the supplied-file path.
The posted verdict shows every recorded criterion, including criteria cited by no finding.

obligations.statement: The whole-repository CI gate validates every tracked attack record without mutating the checkout.

parts.statement: The gate invokes the source-tree checker with `--implementation-started` for every tracked record.
The gate reports every invalid tracked record and its cause in one run.
Missing checker or failed inventory enumeration prevents success.
The gate ignores records outside the tracked checkout and passes an empty inventory when the checker is available.
Repeated runs over an unchanged checkout return the same result.
Passing and failing runs leave tracked, untracked, and ignored files unchanged.
Existing committed records are migrated before a new required lens is enforced on the default branch.

obligations.statement: Adoption uses the installed facade at a sufficient semantic version and preserves tool ownership and handoff boundaries.

parts.statement: Consumers establish a sufficient installed semantic version before using new verbs, refuse named version failures, and do not mutate item state during the check.
Facade delivery is complete only when the installed command reports the required version.
Render, attest, claim, and delivery changes belong to the workcli repository.
The attack and review skills remain Claude-only.
Other tools hand attack and review rounds to Claude Code through the existing delivery workflow.
Dispatch briefs cite the quality standard and amendment-before-use rule.

obligations.statement: Verification uses the prescribed public seams, repository fixtures, and non-mutating test environments.

parts.statement: Tests use the workcli fake backend, exercise rendering through its public verb, and parse output with existing consumers.
Review freshness uses controlled revisions and CI tests use temporary repositories covering the named record states.
No test deploys configuration.
No test rewrites the user's tracker.
Component child specs define wire formats and fixtures before scaffolding.
Child specs retain parent contracts and invariants and leave no significant product decision to implementation.

obligations.statement: Delivery follows the ordered slice and continuation workflow.

parts.statement: Slices are delivered in the stated dependency order.
Each resulting feature is promoted with `work promote` before implementation.
Each promoted spec container holds a design child and blocked implementation placeholder.
The child spec supplies its implementation manifest and dependencies.
A parent outcome spanning slices has a named verification child.
Delivering design does not discharge parent criteria or change their open evidence rows.

ground.reason: LIFE-D5 promises that claim and delivery refuse an otherwise eligible leaf only for the listed acceptance conditions. LIFE-A24 names a finite positive fixture as its check. That fixture cannot distinguish this promise from an implementation that rejects another valid criterion form.

objections.objection: The named fixture can pass even though claim or delivery has an additional, undocumented refusal condition.
objections.obligation: Otherwise eligible noun-bearing leaves are refused only for empty or unresolvable criteria or a required attestation that is not current.

scenario.given: An implementation accepts every noun and wording variant listed in LIFE-A24 but rejects another valid rendering, such as one combining Markdown, non-ASCII text, and multiple sentences.
scenario.when: The LIFE-A24 check claims and delivers only the listed fixtures.
scenario.expect: The fixture passes, while an otherwise eligible leaf containing a valid combination not represented by the fixture is incorrectly refused.

ground.reason: LIFE-D1 promises that the workcli and spec-lint grammars remain counterparts across repositories. LIFE-A28 checks only that both parsers produce the same entries for one shared fixture. Agreement on that artifact does not establish grammar compatibility for other valid inputs.

objections.objection: Two incompatible parsers can satisfy the shared-fixture comparison.
objections.obligation: The workcli and spec-lint grammars remain compatible across repositories.

scenario.given: Both parsers agree on every entry in the shared fixture but disagree on a valid input outside that fixture.
scenario.when: LIFE-A28 runs only the shared round-trip fixture through both parsers.
scenario.expect: The shared-fixture check passes while the parsers produce different entries for another valid document.

ground.reason: LIFE-D4 says amended criteria must be attacked again before use and expressly applies that doctrine to dispatch briefs. LIFE-A32 checks only that a brief cites the quality standard and the rule. Prompt content does not establish that the recipient follows it.

objections.objection: A dispatch brief can contain both required citations while amended criteria are used without another attack.
objections.obligation: A dispatch using amended criteria waits until those criteria have been attacked again.

scenario.given: A dispatch brief contains the required citations but its recipient does not perform the required attack.
scenario.when: The brief is checked for the cited text and then dispatched.
scenario.expect: Inspection of the brief passes while implementation begins from amended, unattacked criteria.

ground.reason: LIFE-A36 says two runs report the same result, but neither it nor the testing decisions define what constitutes the result or equality: exit status, diagnostic set, ordering, or exact output. The document therefore supplies no rule that separates pass from fail.

objections.objection: A checker can declare repeatability from equal exit codes even when the reports differ observably.
objections.obligation: Repeated CI-gate runs over an unchanged checkout have a defined, repeatable result.

scenario.given: Two runs over the same checkout return the same exit status but emit different diagnostics.
scenario.when: LIFE-A36 is evaluated using exit status as the unspecified meaning of result.
scenario.expect: An exit-code comparison passes while diagnostic order or content differs, because the required equality is undefined.

ground.reason: LIFE-D4 says the amended document is attacked again before use, including after a criteria-indicting review halt. LIFE-A40 checks only that subsequent instructions cite that rule and the quality standard. A sentence in instructions does not establish the required workflow outcome.

objections.objection: Review-halt instructions can contain both citations while the amended criteria are reused without another attack.
objections.obligation: Criteria amended after a criteria-indicting review halt are attacked again before use.

scenario.given: The post-halt instructions contain both required citations, but the recipient resumes with the amended criteria without performing the attack.
scenario.when: LIFE-A40 checks the instructions for those citations.
scenario.expect: The instruction-content check passes while the next workflow step uses the amended criteria without another attack.

ground.reason: The document says, "There is no separate editable review copy," but no criterion checks that such a copy is absent or cannot become another authority.

objections.objection: The implementation can introduce an editable review copy while still passing every criterion.

scenario.given: All rendering, emission, and posting checks satisfy LIFE-A1 through LIFE-A44.
scenario.when: The implementation also stores an independently editable criteria copy for review.
scenario.expect: Every criterion still passes although the document's single-authority design is violated.

ground.reason: LIFE-D1 requires the workcli and spec-lint grammars to "remain marked counterparts." LIFE-A28 checks only their behavior on a fixture.

objections.objection: Nothing checks the required counterpart markers.

scenario.given: Both parsers produce identical entries for the shared fixture.
scenario.when: Their required counterpart markers are removed.
scenario.expect: LIFE-A28 and every other criterion pass while the marker obligation is unmet.

ground.reason: LIFE-D1 calls grammar compatibility across repositories an obligation. LIFE-A28 samples only the shared fixture and therefore covers only the constructs represented by that fixture.

objections.objection: The two grammars can disagree on a valid construct absent from the fixture.

scenario.given: The parsers agree on every entry in the shared round-trip fixture.
scenario.when: They parse another valid entry form that the fixture does not contain.
scenario.expect: They return different entries while all stated criteria still pass.

ground.reason: LIFE-D1 says component specs define the exact generated-ID spelling and refusal payloads. No criterion checks that those decisions are present in the component specs.

objections.objection: Implementation can begin with the generated-ID and refusal wire formats still undecided.

scenario.given: Generated IDs satisfy the broad stability and grammar properties in LIFE-A2, and refusals satisfy LIFE-A3.
scenario.when: The component specs omit the exact ID spelling and refusal payload formats.
scenario.expect: All criteria pass while those required design decisions remain in implementation.

ground.reason: LIFE-D2 says, "editing the generated file is not an amendment." No criterion exercises a direct edit and observes that classification.

objections.objection: The workflow may treat a direct edit of the generated rendering as an amendment.

scenario.given: The item, its acceptance field, and its named spec are unchanged.
scenario.when: A user directly edits the committed generated rendering.
scenario.expect: The system can classify the edit as an amendment and require a new attack while all criteria still pass.

ground.reason: LIFE-D3 requires the attestation marker to contain a parseable timestamp. LIFE-A6 checks only that one attestation exists for the content revision.

objections.objection: A marker without a parseable timestamp can satisfy the criteria.

scenario.given: A valid closed record produces one idempotent attestation bound to the current content.
scenario.when: The marker omits its timestamp or writes an unparseable timestamp.
scenario.expect: LIFE-A6 through LIFE-A10 still pass although the marker violates LIFE-D3.

ground.reason: LIFE-D3 requires the marker to contain "the digest of the attacked document's bytes." The criteria require content binding but never observe that exact representation.

objections.objection: An attestation can use another revision token instead of the required byte digest.

scenario.given: The implementation correctly invalidates attestations whenever attacked content changes.
scenario.when: It stores a database revision identifier rather than the digest of the document bytes.
scenario.expect: All behavioral criteria pass while the required marker representation is absent.

ground.reason: LIFE-D3 says the facade "does not duplicate the checker's semantic or lens judgments." No criterion distinguishes that design from a facade that reruns those judgments.

objections.objection: The facade can duplicate semantic or lens evaluation.

scenario.given: The checker succeeds and all binding and closure conditions are valid.
scenario.when: The facade independently reruns semantic and lens judgments before attesting.
scenario.expect: Every criterion passes despite the duplicated responsibility.

ground.reason: LIFE-D4 requires field amendments to use the existing `work acceptance set --why` trail. No criterion inspects that trail.

objections.objection: Acceptance text can be amended without recording the required reason trail.

scenario.given: An amended contract is rerendered, re-attacked, and re-attested before use.
scenario.when: The acceptance field is changed without `--why` or an equivalent recorded trail.
scenario.expect: All lifecycle criteria pass while the amendment-trail obligation is unmet.

ground.reason: LIFE-D5 says creation and discovery may hold rough or empty criteria. No criterion checks those operations.

objections.objection: Creation or discovery can reject rough or empty criteria.

scenario.given: Every gated claim, review, posting, and delivery transition behaves as specified.
scenario.when: A user creates or discovers an item with empty criteria.
scenario.expect: The operation may be refused while every acceptance criterion still passes.

ground.reason: LIFE-D5 guarantees that installing the facade does not rewrite existing items. No criterion observes installation against existing data.

objections.objection: Facade installation can rewrite existing work items.

scenario.given: Existing items later pass the rendering and transition checks.
scenario.when: The facade is installed over a repository containing existing items.
scenario.expect: The installer can rewrite those items while all criteria still pass.

ground.reason: LIFE-D5 requires empty-criteria refusals to name `work acceptance set` and missing-attestation refusals to name the attack step. LIFE-A33 checks those remedies only for claim and delivery; LIFE-A16 and LIFE-A17 require only a cause.

objections.objection: Review emission and verdict posting can omit the prescribed remedy.

scenario.given: Review emission or posting correctly refuses an empty rendering or missing attestation and names the immediate cause.
scenario.when: The refusal omits `work acceptance set` or the attack step.
scenario.expect: LIFE-A16 and LIFE-A17 pass although LIFE-D5's remediation requirement is unmet.

ground.reason: LIFE-D5 says an implementation placeholder "is retired when the spec manifest expands." LIFE-A25 checks only that it is unclaimable.

objections.objection: An implementation placeholder may remain after the manifest expands.

scenario.given: The placeholder is correctly refused at claim.
scenario.when: The spec manifest expands into implementation work.
scenario.expect: The placeholder remains active while all criteria still pass.

ground.reason: LIFE-D6 requires review emission to refuse a failure to obtain the current rendering and never fall back to an unchecked file. LIFE-A16 does not state that dependency-failure behavior.

objections.objection: Review emission can use an unchecked fallback when fresh rendering fails.

scenario.given: The review input would match the current contract if rendering succeeded.
scenario.when: The facade fails to return a fresh rendering.
scenario.expect: The emitter uses a supplied or cached file and emits the round while all explicit LIFE-A16 cases still pass.

ground.reason: LIFE-D6 imposes the same rendering-failure and no-fallback guarantee on verdict posting. LIFE-A17 does not state that case.

objections.objection: Verdict posting can use an unchecked fallback when fresh rendering fails.

scenario.given: The verdict criteria match the round's recorded input.
scenario.when: The poster cannot obtain a fresh rendering.
scenario.expect: The poster falls back to a cached or supplied file and posts while all explicit LIFE-A17 comparisons still pass.

ground.reason: LIFE-D7 requires the whole-repository gate to invoke the source-tree checker with `--implementation-started`. LIFE-A18 checks reported outcomes, not that checker and mode.

objections.objection: The CI gate can reproduce the expected reports without invoking the required checker mode.

scenario.given: A custom validator reports every fixture classified as invalid by LIFE-A18.
scenario.when: The CI gate runs without the source-tree attack checker or without `--implementation-started`.
scenario.expect: LIFE-A18 through LIFE-A20 pass while the specified checker integration is absent.

ground.reason: LIFE-D7 requires existing committed records to be updated before a new required lens is enforced on the default branch. No criterion covers that migration ordering.

objections.objection: A required lens can be enabled before existing records are migrated.

scenario.given: The checker correctly uses its current required-lens registry.
scenario.when: A new lens is enforced on the default branch before committed records are updated.
scenario.expect: CI turns red for all old records while every acceptance criterion still passes.

ground.reason: LIFE-D8 assigns render, attest, claim, and delivery changes to the workcli repository. No criterion checks component ownership.

objections.objection: Those changes can be implemented in another repository or layer.

scenario.given: Every public behavior and version check passes.
scenario.when: Render, attest, claim, or delivery logic is implemented outside workcli.
scenario.expect: All criteria pass despite violating the stated ownership boundary.

ground.reason: LIFE-D8 preserves the attack and review skills as Claude-only. No criterion checks their deployment scope.

objections.objection: The skills can be deployed directly to other tools.

scenario.given: Attack and review behavior satisfies every lifecycle criterion.
scenario.when: The skills are also installed as native assets for Codex, Gemini, or OpenCode.
scenario.expect: All criteria pass while the Claude-only preservation guarantee is violated.

ground.reason: LIFE-D8 says other tools hand attack and review rounds to a Claude Code session through the existing delivery workflow. No criterion exercises that handoff.

objections.objection: A non-Claude tool can fail to hand the round to Claude Code.

scenario.given: The lifecycle works when invoked directly from Claude Code.
scenario.when: Another supported tool reaches an attack or review round.
scenario.expect: No handoff occurs while every criterion still passes.

ground.reason: The Testing decisions require use of the workcli fake backend, the public render verb, and existing spec-lint and verdict consumers. No criterion inspects those test seams.

objections.objection: Tests can bypass the prescribed public interfaces and consumers.

scenario.given: Tests produce passing results for LIFE-A1 through LIFE-A44.
scenario.when: They call private renderer functions with a bespoke parser instead of the fake backend, public verb, and existing consumers.
scenario.expect: All criteria pass while the required testing approach is absent.

ground.reason: The Testing decisions require controlled item revisions for review freshness and temporary Git repositories for the CI cases. No criterion requires those setups.

objections.objection: Freshness and CI tests can omit the prescribed controlled revisions and repository states.

scenario.given: A test suite claims coverage of review freshness and CI behavior.
scenario.when: It uses mocks that never create controlled revisions or temporary repositories with tracked, ignored, missing, and malformed records.
scenario.expect: The acceptance checks can pass without the required integration setups.

ground.reason: The Testing decisions state, "No test deploys configuration." No criterion preserves that safety boundary.

objections.objection: A lifecycle test may deploy configuration.

scenario.given: The test suite establishes every behavioral criterion.
scenario.when: One test invokes a real configuration deployment as setup.
scenario.expect: All criteria pass despite violating the test safety guarantee.

ground.reason: The Testing decisions also state that no test rewrites the user's tracker. No criterion observes the user's tracker before and after the suite.

objections.objection: A lifecycle test may mutate the user's tracker.

scenario.given: All test assertions pass.
scenario.when: A test uses the real tracker and rewrites an item.
scenario.expect: The suite remains green while the preservation guarantee is violated.

ground.reason: The Testing decisions require component child specs to define wire formats and fixtures before scaffolding. No criterion checks either their content or timing.

objections.objection: Scaffolding can start before wire formats and fixtures are defined.

scenario.given: The eventual implementation satisfies all parent criteria.
scenario.when: Scaffolding begins while the child spec still lacks wire formats or fixtures.
scenario.expect: Every criterion can pass although the specified design-before-scaffolding order was violated.

ground.reason: The Testing decisions require child specs to retain the public contracts, not weaken parent invariants, and not leave significant product decisions to implementation. No criterion reviews child specs against those constraints.

objections.objection: A child spec can weaken an invariant or defer a significant decision.

scenario.given: The implemented examples happen to satisfy all parent criteria.
scenario.when: A child spec narrows a parent invariant or leaves a material wire decision to the implementer.
scenario.expect: All criteria pass while the child-spec constraint is unmet.

ground.reason: The Ordered slice list establishes dependency ordering, including S2 after S1, S3 after S2, and later consumers after S3. No criterion checks the order in which slices are delivered.

objections.objection: Slices can be implemented out of the specified order.

scenario.given: The final combined implementation satisfies LIFE-A1 through LIFE-A44.
scenario.when: S4 or S6 is delivered before the attack path in S3.
scenario.expect: All final criteria pass although the ordered delivery obligation was violated.

ground.reason: The Continuations section instructs, "Use `work promote` on each resulting feature before implementation." No criterion observes that promotion.

objections.objection: Implementation can begin without promoting the feature.

scenario.given: A feature ultimately satisfies its assigned lifecycle criteria.
scenario.when: Work begins without first running `work promote`.
scenario.expect: All acceptance checks pass while the required tracker transition never occurred.

ground.reason: The Continuations section requires each promoted spec container to hold a design child and a blocked implementation placeholder. No criterion checks that topology.

objections.objection: A promoted feature can lack the required design child or blocked placeholder.

scenario.given: The feature's implementation satisfies all assigned criteria.
scenario.when: Its spec container contains only an implementation item.
scenario.expect: All criteria pass while the required tracker structure is absent.

ground.reason: The Continuations section requires the child spec to supply the implementation manifest and the listed dependencies. No criterion checks either.

objections.objection: A child spec can omit its implementation manifest or dependency declarations.

scenario.given: The implementation happens to complete successfully.
scenario.when: The child spec contains no implementation manifest or does not name the ordered-slice dependencies.
scenario.expect: All lifecycle criteria pass while the continuation contract is incomplete.

ground.reason: The Continuations section requires a verification child for any parent outcome spanning slices. No criterion checks that such a child exists.

objections.objection: A cross-slice parent outcome can have no verification child.

scenario.given: A parent outcome depends on work delivered by multiple slices.
scenario.when: The child spec creates no verification child for that outcome.
scenario.expect: Every acceptance criterion can still pass without the required cross-slice evidence owner.

ground.reason: The Continuations section guarantees that delivering the design does not discharge parent criteria or change their open evidence rows. No criterion observes those rows after design delivery.

objections.objection: Design delivery can incorrectly close parent evidence.

scenario.given: A design child is delivered before implementation evidence exists.
scenario.when: The tracker marks one or more parent criteria discharged or changes their evidence rows from open.
scenario.expect: All product criteria remain capable of passing although the evidence-lifecycle guarantee is violated.

ground.reason: LIFE-A13 requires PR delivery to refuse "a leaf" with empty or unresolvable criteria, with no noun-bearing qualifier, while LIFE-A15 requires a design child to pass delivery without the criteria gate. LIFE-D5 states a design child remains outside claim and delivery gates, which supports the A15 reading, but A13's wording (unlike A11, which does say "noun-bearing leaf") leaves open whether a design child counts as "a leaf" it refuses. One reading refuses the delivery; the other lets it pass.

objections.objection: A design child with empty criteria can be either refused or passed at PR delivery depending on whether A13's unqualified "a leaf" is read to include design children, so an implementation can satisfy one criterion while violating the other under a defensible reading.

scenario.given: A design child of a spec container whose acceptance field is empty, delivered with --pr
scenario.when: The delivery gate is evaluated against LIFE-A13 and LIFE-A15
scenario.expect: Under A13 read literally, delivery is refused for empty criteria; under A15, delivery passes without the criteria gate. The two verdicts conflict on the same transition.

ground.reason: LIFE-D1 says only 'Resolve relative spec paths from the repository root'; it never states whether an absolute path or a relative path escaping the root is a refused reference. LIFE-A3's refusal cases (unresolved ID, ID collision, missing/unreadable/unparseable spec) do not include a readable spec file that lives outside the repository, so no criterion tests it and no decision rules it out.

objections.objection: The criteria let an item name a spec outside the repository root, making the canonical contract depend on bytes that fresh checkouts, CI, and other machines cannot reproduce — undermining the document's purpose of an authoritative, revision-bound contract — with no defined refusal.

scenario.given: a work item whose named spec path is absolute, or relative with '..' segments resolving outside the repository root, pointing at a readable, parseable spec file
scenario.when: work acceptance render ID runs
scenario.expect: a named refusal of the out-of-repository spec path (or an explicit decision that such paths are allowed); no criterion checks either outcome

ground.reason: LIFE-A27 tests that editing a cited entry changes the rendering, but the inverse boundary is untested: LIFE-D4's conservative rule ('changing a spec's bytes invalidates... every spec-born item's attestation') names only spec-born items, and no criterion pins whether a tracker-born item citing the spec keeps its rendering byte-equal and its attestation current when the edit touches only uncited entries. Digest binding in LIFE-D3 implies it survives; the invalidation prose invites the opposite reading.

objections.objection: The criteria leave untested whether an editorial spec change outside cited entries forces citing tracker-born items through a new attack round or leaves their renderings and attestations untouched — a divergence that decides whether every spec typo fix invalidates unrelated items' evidence.

scenario.given: a tracker-born item citing spec entry X, with a committed rendering, a closed record, and a current attestation
scenario.when: the named spec is edited only in entry Y, which the item does not cite
scenario.expect: the item's fresh rendering is byte-equal to the committed one and its attestation remains current; no criterion checks this, and LIFE-D4's 'changing a spec's bytes invalidates' language can be read to demand a full re-attack

ground.reason: LIFE-A25 refuses an implementation placeholder at claim only, while the parallel structural criterion LIFE-A26 refuses its items 'at claim and at delivery'. LIFE-D5's table defines leaf behavior and placeholders are not noun-bearing leaves, so LIFE-A13/A14 do not reach them either; nothing tests or states what happens when PR delivery is invoked on a placeholder directly.

objections.objection: The criteria let PR delivery of an implementation placeholder through untested: the claim refusal can be bypassed by invoking delivery on an item that was never legitimately claimed, and no gate row or criterion names the refusal.

scenario.given: an implementation placeholder under a spec container, never claimed
scenario.when: PR delivery is invoked on it
scenario.expect: a refusal naming the placeholder's structural role as the cause; no criterion checks delivery of a placeholder

dispositions.rationale: A promise that no other refusal exists is a universal negative with no finite check. LIFE-A24's fixture of every noun and varied wording is its checkable form, and PR review of the gate code judges the rest.

Earlier rounds rejected this ground. Agreement on every possible input is a universal claim with no finite check. LIFE-A28 requires the shared fixture to exercise every resolution rule in LIFE-D1, which is the checkable form of that compatibility.

Earlier rounds rejected this ground. The gates enforce use before re-attack: LIFE-A8, A9, A14, A16 and A17 refuse stale or unattested criteria. LIFE-A32 pins only what the brief must say, because the brief text is the interface to the dispatched agent.

The gates enforce use before re-attack: LIFE-A8, A9, A14, A16 and A17 refuse stale or unattested criteria. LIFE-A40 pins only what the halt instructions must say, because that text is the interface to the agent that acts on the halt.
LIFE-A16 and LIFE-A17 refuse any criteria that differ from a fresh rendering, so an editable copy can never become an authority.
Earlier rounds rejected this ground. The counterpart markers are a maintenance device. LIFE-A28 observes the compatibility they protect.
Earlier rounds rejected this ground. Agreement on every possible input has no finite check. LIFE-A28's fixture exercises every resolution rule in LIFE-D1.
The lifecycle's own gates and each child spec's attack round enforce these on the child specs.

Every consuming boundary computes a fresh rendering (LIFE-D3), and LIFE-A7 refuses to attest a tracker-born file that differs from one. An edit to the generated file therefore changes no contract, which is what the sentence promises.
Earlier rounds rejected this ground. Nothing in this spec reads the marker's timestamp, and LIFE-D3 leaves the marker encoding to the facade component spec.
LIFE-D3 leaves the marker's encoding to the facade component spec. LIFE-A6 to A10 observe what the binding must do.
Whether the facade repeats the checker's judgments is placement, judged in PR review. It is not behaviour an acceptance check can observe.
Earlier rounds rejected this ground. The --why trail is existing `work acceptance set` behaviour, and nothing in this spec changes it.
Creation and discovery accepting rough criteria is existing behaviour, and no slice here changes those verbs.
Earlier rounds rejected this ground. No slice includes a migration, so no implementation step could rewrite existing items.
Earlier rounds rejected this ground. Placeholder retirement is existing facade behaviour (`work deliver --spec` reconciles a design child's placeholder), and this spec does not change it.
